$comment: THE central registry of accounts the bench uses. Specs resolve accounts through
src/fixtures/test-accounts.ts and never hard-code a KPost ID.
NO PASSWORDS LIVE IN THIS FILE. It is committed to the repository, so every credential is a
POINTER to an environment variable (`passwordEnv`) rather than the secret itself. A password
written here would be in the git history permanently, readable by anyone with repo access, and
could not be rotated by changing a deployment.
`provisioned: false` means the account DOES NOT EXIST on the target yet. Specs that need it
report SKIPPED with that reason; they never fall back to another account, because a test that
silently runs as somebody else is worse than one that does not run.
To add an account: create it on the target, then set `provisioned: true` and record
`provisionedAt`. `npm run accounts:verify` reconciles this file against the database.

rationale: KPost separates account types by e-mail domain, and the signup UI binds the domain from the
user type rather than letting the user type it. Verified against KPOST_QA (active accounts):
PERSONAL   @kpost.in        205   ← LEGACY, predates the split (e.g. QA_KPOST_ID)
BUSINESS_* <slug>.kpost.in  603   ← companies that registered their own sub-domain
So a personal account on @kpost.in is not invalid data — it is old data. Bench-owned accounts
follow the current policy so they exercise the path the product actually routes new users
down; the legacy accounts stay usable and are flagged, not rewritten, because rewriting a
kpost_id is a primary-key change across ~90 tables.
Business accounts use the BARE domain rather than a per-company sub-domain: a sub-domain is
issued when a company registers one, which is a separate flow this registry does not drive.

accounts.purpose: The bench's own account: the sender in 1:1 flows and the caller for profile reads.
The receiver in 1:1 Katchup and KMail flows, and the second session for isolation probes.
A third party: Cc, confidential-copy invisibility (NFR-SEC02) and group membership of three.
Administrator of the test business company; drives the Admin permission workflows.
An ordinary member of the test company: the subject of permission and role checks.
The member Admin flows may terminate or hold. Expendable by design — never reuse it elsewhere.
